body:
Triage(决策箱勤务):补标准四棱卡面块 —— 卡内测量完整,此块为收件箱标准件。

① **项目长远合理性**:#5155 已裁「拒收活在 zod/publish 边界」,所以镜像层就是作者契约的权威声明 —— 两种方言并存等于契约自相矛盾;裁定其一(或把「分面共存」写成工具可读的规则)都收敛,不裁则这一族每张后续卡都要从 56:11 的票数里重新猜。
② **实际业务拉动**:11 个 `z.string()` 镜像今天在广告一个 runtime 丢弃的能力 —— #4453 实测:作者写的 handler 表达式被 `typeof === 'function'` 静默 drop。写了白写、无声无息,正是这一族要关的洞。
③ **防 AI 写代码犯错**:`z.function()` 对任何序列化文档不可满足(声明即不可作者化);若意图是表达式方言,56 个 function 镜像又挡住合法作者。现状同时教 AI 两套矛盾拼法 —— 哪个方向都比「不裁」强。
④ **创业阶段不扩散需求**:裁 function-only 是收缩(11 个镜像走退役路线);裁表达式方言是大新面(#6152 的 23 键各要加表达式位 + 解析执行机制)。从紧默认前者,除非有真实作者场景拉动。
推荐:**function-only**(11 个 `z.string()` 镜像按退役路线处理,#6152 的 23 键维持 runtime-only 重分类);「分面共存」仅当维护者明确要 authored-handler 能力,且须成文为工具可读规则。
置信缺口:out-of-tree corpus 里是否已有作者在写 handler 表达式(未测);spec 侧对应键的方言(若有)未在本席核对。

<!-- os-decision-facets -->

Maintainer ruling (2026-08-25, batch adjudication, batch 4; verbatim: 「同意」): **Option A — the handler-expression string dialect is NOT a supported authoring form.** The contract, coherent with the same-day #6124-A ruling: the authorable form for actions is the declarative ActionDef object; runtime callbacks are the programmatic face (function arm / runtime-only). Consequences ruled with it:

- The **11 `z.string()` handler mirrors** join #6124's per-key sweep with the same treatment: renderer consumes a declarative object form ⇒ `z.union([z.function(), <ActionDef>])`; otherwise runtime-only retirement. They stop advertising an expression capability the runtime measurably drops (#4453).
- **#6152's 23 keys stay runtime-only** — its ruling stands unchanged.
- The rule is now stated where tools can read it (this ruling + the #6124 ruling comment); no future card re-derives the dialect from a 56:11 vote.

State transition: `needs-user-decision` → `pm:blocked` with `Blocked-by: #6124` — this card closes when the sweep lands and a re-verification shows the 11 mirrors no longer carry the bare `z.string()` expression dialect (re-run the card's own `rg` on the merged ref). Relabeled `domain:ui` (the close-condition surface is `packages/types`). Scope-extension note posted on #6124.

## Half-state repaired: `Blocked-by: #6124` lifted into the body

The 2026-08-25 maintainer ruling set this card's state transition (`needs-user-decision` → `pm:blocked` with `Blocked-by: #6124`) **in a comment only**. The label moved; the machine-readable line never landed. That makes the card invisible to the reverse index the unlock scan runs on, so it could not be put back when #6124's sweep lands — one of 17 such cards measured across this lane (#6653).

Repaired, with no substance changed:

- `Blocked-by: #6124` as the first line.
- The ruling quoted at the top, so a reader does not have to reach the second comment to learn the question is **answered** — the body still opened with "this cannot be read off the code / the seat is not guessing it", which now reads as though the decision were outstanding.
- The consequences the ruling fixed are folded into the two sections that previously listed them as open alternatives, and the `rg` at the bottom is labelled as what it now is: the card's **close condition**, to be run on the merged ref.

Verified while repairing: **#6124 is open, `pm:queue`, `domain:ui`, unassigned** — so the block is live and correctly held. It is also a dispatchable card in this lane with its direction already ruled, which this seat has noted as a refill candidate.

Close condition re-run on the merged ref (`origin/main` = `2956d7af8`, after PR #7339 closed #6124 at 09:04Z) — **not met**. The card's own `rg` returns 14 `on*` sites: **0** `z.function()` (PR #7339 swept all 58), **11** `z.string()`, **3** `z.any()`.

Of the 11 `z.string()` sites, three are event NAMES by ruling (PR #6899; `views.zod.ts:152` `onViewChange`, `:177` `onChange`, `:197` `onChange`, each described as "an event NAME, not a callback or a handler expression") and are outside this card's dialect question. The remaining 8 (`app.zod.ts:205`, `blocks.zod.ts:108,109,122,123`, `reports.zod.ts:170,171`, `views.zod.ts:117`) plus the 3 `z.any()` (`crud.zod.ts:105,145,160`) are the per-key treatment the 2026-08-25 ruling assigned to #6124's sweep. PR #7339's census was anchored on `z.function()` sites and never contained them, so #6124 closed with this half unexecuted.

Filed **#7344** as the execution card for that residual (Clause-② yes, `pm:queue`, `domain:ui`, p2), with the sites tabled and the treatment fixed to the #6124 shape. This card stays `pm:blocked`; the body's first line now reads `Blocked-by: #7344` (edited in place; the two other edits are the bracketed "residual: #7344" notes and the Refs line — no substance changed). It closes when #7344 lands and the `rg` above returns only the three event-name keys.

## ✅ Close condition MET — re-verified on the merged ref, with a temporal control

`domain:ui` PM seat, session `session_01EMrWaQw3XS5DxTHxp4yRyC`. This card's close condition is executable and I ran it rather than inferring it from the sweep card's closure.

> This card closes when that sweep lands and a re-verification shows the 11 mirrors no longer carry the bare `z.string()` expression dialect — re-run the `rg` at the bottom of this card **on the merged ref**.

Two conjuncts. Both measured.

### Conjunct 1 — the sweep landed

#7344 (the residual after PR #7339) is **closed `completed` 2026-09-03T08:50:52Z**. Read directly, not taken from a scan's summary of it.

### Conjunct 2 — the re-verification, on `origin/main` `2099df405`

| dialect, anchored to an `on*` key in `packages/types/src/zod/` | this card measured (2026-08-24) | now |
|---|---:|---:|
| `z.function()` | 56 | **0** |
| `z.string()` | 11 | **3** |
| `z.any()` | 3 | **0** |

And the **3** survivors are not the expression dialect. All three are `views.zod.ts` event-name keys — `onViewChange:157`, `onChange:182`, `onChange:202` — and all three carry the disambiguating describe verbatim:

> `Event name dispatched on window when the view changes (detail: { view }) — an event NAME, not a callback or a handler expression`

(3 of 3 carry that exact clause; counted, not eyeballed.) These are the keys #7344 explicitly excluded by ruling, and its own close condition #4 anticipated this exact result: *"returns only the three event-name keys."*

Per-key, over the eight names this card named:

| key | still in the `z.string()` handler dialect | present in any dialect |
|---|---:|---:|
| `onClick` | 0 | 9 |
| `onInstall` | 0 | 0 |
| `onPreview` | 0 | 0 |
| `onSave` | 0 | 1 |
| `onCancel` | 0 | 3 |
| `onBack` | 0 | 2 |
| `onViewChange` | **1** (event-name) | 2 |
| `onChange` | **2** (event-name) | 19 |

The keys did not vanish — they took the ruled treatment. Sampled: `onClick: handlerKeyRefusal('onClick', 'runtime-slot', 'Click handler')`, `onSave: handlerKeyRefusal('onSave', 'retired', 'Save callback')`. That is the `handlerKeyRefusal` shape #6124's ruling fixed, applied per key with a `retired` / `runtime-slot` disposition — ⇒ the outcome exceeds this card's condition rather than merely satisfying it (the three `z.any()` mirrors went too, and this card only asked about the `z.string()` eleven).

### ⭐ Controls, because three of those cells are zeros

**Control A — same directory, same instrument.** `z.function` is *not* absent from `packages/types/src/zod/`: it occurs 7 times across 5 files (`base.zod.ts:407` `EventHandlersSchema`, `data-display.zod.ts:123` `cell` / `:280` `renderCellEditor`, `form.zod.ts:148` `validate` / `:159` `custom`, plus two comments). The probe finds those; it returns 0 only under the `on*`-key anchoring. ⇒ the zero is a reading, not a dead pattern. It is also the *correct* zero: #7344's ruling fenced those four non-`on*` sites as out of scope (Q4 → B), and they are exactly the four still standing.

**Control B — temporal.** The identical command walked back over this repo's own history:

| ref | date | `z.function()` | `z.string()` | `z.any()` |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `main~400` `d0889e2f1` | 2026-08-28 | **56** | 11 | 3 |
| `main~250` `c0c436db8` | 2026-08-31 | 58 | 11 | 3 |
| `main~150` `3561bd2ca` | 2026-09-01 | 58 | 11 | 3 |
| `main~80` `bb459ea9c` | 2026-09-02 | **0** | 11 | 3 |
| `main~40` `e8c553bcb` | 2026-09-03 | 0 | **3** | **0** |
| `origin/main` `2099df405` | today | 0 | 3 | 0 |

⭐ `main~400` reproduces **this card's own 56 / 11 / 3 census**, four days and ~400 commits ago, from the same one-line command. The probe demonstrably fires non-zero on older refs of the same tree — so today's zeros cannot be a broken instrument. The two step changes are visible and land where the record says they should: PR #7339 between `~150` and `~80`, PR #7468 between `~80` and `~40`.

### ⚠️ One instrument defect in this card's own `rg`, recorded so the next reader is not misled

The pattern at the bottom of this card is unanchored, so it matches `on[A-Z]` as a **substring**. Run verbatim today it returns **12** hits, of which **9 are false positives** — `acti**onN**ame`, `conversati**onI**d`, `acti**onU**rl`, `butt**onL**abel` ×2, `butt**onT**ext`, `locati**onF**ield` ×2, `descripti**onF**ield`. Only 3 are `on*` keys.

⇒ A seat re-running it and reading "12" as twelve surviving handler mirrors would re-open this card wrongly. Anchor it:

```
rg -n '^\s*on[A-Z][A-Za-z]*:\s*z\.(function|string|any)' packages/types/src/zod/
```

Immaterial to the verdict (the anchored count is what all figures above use), recorded because this family's whole subject is instruments that quietly return the wrong population.

### Disposition

**Closing as `completed`.** The ruling (2026-08-25, Option A) was already recorded; the sweep it assigned has landed and the re-verification passes.

⚠️ **This unblocks #6497** (`Blocked-by: #6182`) — handled on that card separately, ⛔ **not** re-queued on the strength of this closure alone: a discharged `Blocked-by:` is necessary, never sufficient, and #6497 carries its own re-verification precondition plus a second gate. See my comment there.
